subject.title: [Feature]: Add tools.web.fetch.allowPrivateNetwork to allow private network access

question: Should OpenClaw expose broad private-network access for arbitrary `web_fetch` URLs, and should the public API be a nested/per-agent `ssrfPolicy.dangerouslyAllowPrivateNetwork` contract instead of the requested top-level key?
rationale: The source shows the implementation primitive exists, but exposing it changes the SSRF trust boundary and the current discussion has not settled the permanent public contract.

options.title: Adopt nested audited policy
options.body: Use `tools.web.fetch.ssrfPolicy` and optionally per-agent overrides with dangerous naming, audit output, docs, and targeted security tests.

options.title: Add simple global opt-in
options.body: Expose a top-level or global broad boolean and accept the larger blast radius with clear operator documentation.

options.title: Reject broad private access
options.body: Keep arbitrary `web_fetch` strict and direct users to trusted proxies, narrow fake-IP flags, or purpose-built internal-service tools.

recommendation.title: Adopt nested audited policy
recommendation.body: Use `tools.web.fetch.ssrfPolicy` and optionally per-agent overrides with dangerous naming, audit output, docs, and targeted security tests.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest visible SSRF/web_fetch policy history and already commented on the security-sensitive API shape.
